messages:
anna: thinking aloud — we need a small, auditable shim that translates plan -> enforcement buckets. current system ties rate-limit strictly to plan id and it's hard to support burst credits + per-key overrides. proposal attached in-line.

mike: +1. can we keep it stateless for the fast path?

anna: yes — core idea: token contains plan_id + optional override flags; edge proxies consult shim which is just a policy lookup (in-memory) that returns {limit, burst_window, priority}. no DB lookup on hot path.

sasha: rough sketch of the mapping:
```json
{
  "free": { "qps": 1, "burst_tokens": 10, "burst_window_s": 60 },
  "pro": { "qps": 10, "burst_tokens": 200, "burst_window_s": 60 },
  "enterprise": { "qps": 50, "burst_tokens": 1000, "burst_window_s": 120 }
}
```

sasha: edge will refill burst_tokens using a leaky-bucket per-org or per-key key. per-key overrides (seat-level) can be applied by returning a higher bucket if entitlement exists.

jordan: how do we charge for burst usage in billing? we want predictable invoicing and also allow short spikes without penalizing customers.

anna: plan: bill steady-state usage per-token; bursts are free up to a soft budget per billing period (e.g., monthly). if org exceeds soft budget, we start emitting alerts and throttle to plan qps. beyond hard budget, fallback to rate-limit or require purchase of burst pack.

kevin: we should add a per-org softcap counter in telemetry and an aggregated metric: quota.burst.used and quota.burst.available. quota-bot can post alerts when available < 10%.

quota-bot: automated: Monitoring rule created: "quota.burst.available < 0.1" -> post to #billing-alerts and create incident stub.

mike: operational concerns — for Dedicated and Private, the shim must be configurable via config file or control-plane API. we can't force cloud-only defaults.

anna: agreed. config precedence: control-plane overrides static defaults -> org entitlements -> per-key overrides -> runtime feature flags. document this in the console UX.

sasha: console UX idea: show a plan matrix in billing settings with sliders for QPS and Burst budget; ability to set 'grace window' (how long burst persists) and to toggle 'enforce hard throttle' for free tier.

jordan: we need a migration path for existing customers that currently use custom rate-limits. propose a one-month opt-in where we map old limits to nearest plan and send email with recommended changes.

kevin: edge case: what about multi-org api keys (platform-level keys used by infra)? we should allow per-key override with an allowlist of admin keys. also an emergency bypass token for support with audit logging.

mike: implementation note: keep hot path pure C-ish logic in the proxy layer: lookup -> return numeric limits -> check token bucket. all async calls for reconciliation or usage writes must be best-effort.

anna: question for eng: should the policy return both rate and a policy id so logs can be correlated? that will help A/B rollouts of new plans.

kevin: yes. response shape: {policy_id, qps, burst_tokens, refill_s, priority, billing_tag}. store policy_id in request logs.

sasha: small sample response we can use in tests:
```json
{"policy_id":"plan-pro-v2","qps":10,"burst_tokens":200,"refill_s":60,"priority":50,"billing_tag":"plan:pro"}
```

mike: tests: add unit tests for policy lookup, integration test for proxy with simulated burst refill, chaos run for fallback to lower-tier model under saturation.

jordan: what about exposing per-route limits? some customers want higher qps for embeddings but lower for generate.

anna: propose route-level multipliers in the policy, e.g., embeddings: 2x, generate: 1x. keep multipliers simple to reason about.

sasha: also add a human-readable reason code for throttles in the response header so SDKs can surface user-friendly prompts: e.g., X-Quota-Reason: "burst_exhausted" or "hard_throttle_plan_limit".

kevin: rollout: start with internal tenants -> opt-in partners -> default for new signups -> existing customers with migration emails. metrics after each stage: throttle rate, SRR (support request rate), revenue impact.

mike: who will own the policy definitions? PM + Billing for values, Platform for enforcement. we need a toy UI for finance to tweak values without deploys.

anna: I'll make a short PR for the policy schema and a console mock. target sync next Tue.

jordan: please include the billing math in PR: soft budget thresholds and how overage events translate to invoices or upsell triggers.

sasha: I'll add unit tests and a simulation harness to the repo branch.

kevin: logging checklist: policy_id, returned_limits, token_key, bucket_state_before_after, throttle_reason, request_route. keep logs small but sufficient.

mike: ops checklist: per-region circuit-breaker if global bursting starts to affect tail latency.

anna: great thread. next actions: anna will PR schema, sasha will add tests, jordan will draft billing copy, kevin will mock console sliders, mike will write ops runbook. ping me if blocked. :thumbsup:
